claim: For many small calls, the cost of switching to 28 MHz per call can exceed the saving; use one window around the whole pass.

evidence.text: Running the cell hooks at 28 MHz cut 124 frames to 94, not to the original's 58: a hook called 5,500 times spends most of its time getting there (PC sample by NR 7).
evidence.quote: cut 124 frames to 94, not to the original's 58: a hook called 5,500 times spends most of its time getting there.

evidence.text: A wait per figure cost about 1,600 T of 3.5 MHz time each, more than the 28 MHz saved on a small figure; one window around the whole draw pass fixed it.
